AdminAlertController: Admin composing alerts for selected organizers. Shares the service with the organizer side; only the sender scope differs, which is what decides the audience and how every query is filtered.
AdminRateLimitController: Lets an admin adjust the "auth" rate limit policy (login, refresh-token, 2FA verify) without a redeploy. A change takes effect on the next request - see RateLimitSettingsService for the cache-warming details.
CustomInvoicingModulesController: Lets the platform admin see and switch which modules organizers may author new custom invoices for.
CustomInvoicingModulesController::GetMod: Lists every module that can offer custom invoicing, with its switch and who last changed it. Cancels the request. One entry per offered module in module order; a module never switched reads off with no change details.
CustomInvoicingModulesController::SetEna: Switches custom invoicing on or off for one module. The module name from the route, e.g. Membership. The state the module is switched to. Cancels the request. 200 with the module's resulting state and a message; 400 when the module cannot offer custom invoicing.
NotificationController::GetNotificationD: Retrieves details of a specific notification with all recipients
NotificationController::GetNotificationR: Retrieves recipients of a specific notification with pagination
NotificationController::MarkAsRead: Marks a notification as read for a specific recipient
NotificationController::UpdateRecipientS: Updates the status of a notification recipient
CampaignTeamController: Fundraising teams on a campaign. The two reads are anonymous because a team page is something supporters share with donors; everything that changes a team requires a signed-in caller and is authorised inside the service against their own fundraising page, and the captain-only actions against captaincy of that exact team. Holding a menu item is not what grants access here. The route is absolute rather than area-prefixed so the address a supporter sees in their browser is the address the API answers on, minus /api.
CampaignTeamController::LeaveTeam: Leaving is addressed as "me" rather than by membership identifier, so a caller cannot leave on somebody else's behalf by naming their row.
EmailVerificationController: Confirming a supporter's email address. Anonymous by necessity: the person following the link has not signed in yet, and confirming an address is what stands between them and being able to fundraise. Both actions are rate limited by address, because both spend something real - one puts mail in an inbox, the other is an attempt at a token.
FundraiserInvitationController: The charity's half of invitations: who has been asked, who to ask next, and what the email will look like before it goes. Which campaign a caller may touch is decided inside the service from the token's own organiser, so holding the permission never grants sight of another charity's invitations. Sending is an edit and is gated as one.
FundraiserInvitationLinkController: The invited person's half. Reading an invitation and unsubscribing from one are anonymous by necessity — the holder of the link has not signed in, and an unsubscribe that demanded a password would not be an unsubscribe. Accepting is not: it creates a fundraising page, so it requires an account, and the service checks that account is the one the invitation was sent to.
FundraiserPageController: The public face of a supporter's fundraising page. Anonymous by design - a donor should never have to hold an account to give - so the service behind it returns only what a stranger may see, and every reason a page cannot be shown comes back as the same sentence. The route is absolute rather than prefixed so the address a donor sees in their browser is the address the API answers on, minus /api.
MyFundraisingController: A supporter's own fundraising pages. Every route is addressed by the page's public identifier and authorised against the token's user inside the service, so holding a menu item is not what grants access here - owning the row is. A page belonging to somebody else is refused with the same sentence as a page that does not exist. The route is absolute rather than area-prefixed so the address the supporter sees in their browser is the address the API answers on, minus /api.
PeerToPeerEmailTemplateController: The six lifecycle emails a charity can edit for one campaign. Reading is a view permission and saving is an edit; the campaign a caller may touch is resolved inside the service from the token's own organiser. Sending a test puts mail in an inbox, so it carries the send allowance.
PeerToPeerJoinController: The supporter-facing half of peer-to-peer. Joining is never anonymous: the fundraiser row is owned by the token's user, so there is no caller-supplied identity to forge. No permission policy applies here because any signed-in supporter may fundraise; whether this campaign accepts pages is decided from the campaign row inside the service.
PeerToPeerLeaderboardController: The campaign's fundraising standings. Anonymous by design, because a board a charity publishes is something supporters share with people who hold no account. A board the charity keeps to itself is still served from here, but only to the charity that owns the campaign, and the refusal is the same sentence a stranger gets for a campaign that does not exist. The route is absolute rather than area-prefixed so the address a reader sees in their browser is the address the API answers on, minus /api.
PeerToPeerModerationController: The charity's oversight of what its supporters publish. The permission policies here narrow who may reach these endpoints; which campaign a caller may touch is decided inside the service from the token's own organiser, so holding the permission never grants sight of another charity's pages. Taking something down is an edit, and is gated as one.
PeerToPeerSettingsController: The organiser-facing peer-to-peer switch. Every action authorises on ownership of the campaign inside the service; the permission policies here narrow who may reach it, they do not decide which campaign the caller is allowed to touch.
SupporterSignUpController: The one anonymous write in peer-to-peer. It is kept apart from the join controller rather than added to it as an opt-out, so no future action inherits anonymous access by sitting next to this one. The account it creates is a supporter account under the campaign's charity: it carries no organiser role and provisions no organisation.
EventCartController::CreateCart: The only unauthenticated entry point into registration - every other cart route needs the cart id this returns. A cart holds seats, so unchallenged creation is a seat-denial vector, not just row spam. The capability cookie issued here is what every later cart route is gated on, so the cart id alone is not enough to reach the registration once it has left this browser.
EventCartController::SubmitAnswers: Custom forms and questions are authored on the event, so the buyer answers them once for the whole order rather than once per cart line.
EventCartController::UploadAnswerFile: Anonymous by necessity - the buyer has no account until checkout - so the request budget is capped here as well as by the size and extension rules the service applies.
EventCartController::GetSeating: Everything the seat map needs to draw itself: the workspace public key, the session's Seats.io event, this cart's hold token and what each category costs. The workspace secret key is not among them and never is.
EventCartController::HoldSeat: Claims one seat for this cart. The request names a seat and nothing else: its category, its ticket type and its price are all established on the server, because a browser naming its own category would be naming its own price.
EventCartController::ReleaseSeat: Gives up one of this cart's seats, putting it back on sale for everyone else.
EventCheckoutController::CreatePaymentIn: Reaches Stripe on an anonymous caller's behalf, so it is the card-testing surface of the flow. Challenged separately from cart creation because a wizard can sit open longer than a token lives.
EventCheckoutController::RecordChequePay: Organizer-only: recording a cheque issues tickets while the invoice stays owing, so it must be authenticated rather than anonymous like the rest of checkout.
EventOrderController: The buyer-facing view of one placed order. Anonymous and guarded only by the unguessable invoice id, matching the ticket view page. Rate limited because it is both anonymous and polled: the confirmation page asks again every few seconds while a bank payment settles.
EventRegistrationController::GetEventReg: What one session's seat map needs to draw itself before the buyer has a cart: the workspace public key, the session's Seats.io event and what each category costs. It carries no hold token, so the chart it draws can be read but no seat claimed against it - holding a seat needs a cart and stays on the cart routes.
EventRegistrationController::IssueEventR: Gives the seat map the token it holds seats under before the buyer has a cart. The form asks for a name and email a step after it shows the seats, and a cart cannot open without them, so without this the chart could be looked at but not picked on. The token holds nothing by itself; a seat still leaves inventory only through the cart routes, which take the token over once the cart opens. A browser that already holds one presents it and keeps it, so reloading the page does not strand the seats it picked behind a token nobody holds any more. Whether the presented token still holds anything is settled with Seats.io, never taken on the browser's word.
EventRegistrationController::ExtendEvent: Pushes the buyer's hold token expiry out while they are still choosing, so the seats the chart shows as held stay held. The token minted when the chart first opened lasts a fixed span and Seats.io does not renew it as the buyer works, so without this a buyer who lingers finds their seats freed and every pick refused. It extends the existing token rather than minting a new one, so the seats already held are never let go.
EventRegistrationController::ReleaseEven: Puts seats back on sale that the buyer picked on the chart before they had a cart. The chart holds every seat picked on it under the token it was given, and draws those seats as chosen again under the same token, so a seat taken out of the basket while the map is closed has to be given back here. The presented token is what proves the caller may free these seats: Seats.io releases only what that token holds.
EventTicketViewController: The buyer-facing view of a single issued ticket. Anonymous and guarded only by the unguessable ticket id, matching how the membership invoice view already works - the same page is what the PDF renderer loads.
LoadTestSeedController: Builds and tears down the fixture a load harness races against. Authenticated as an organizer even though the routes only exist off production: the seeded event is created under whoever is calling, and the harness needs that same identity afterwards to record a cheque against it.
CustomInvoicePayController: The buyer's pay page for a custom invoice, whatever module it bills. Anonymous: the unguessable invoice id in the link the organizer sends is the only credential, matching the order status and ticket view pages. Every action is rate limited per address because nothing else identifies the caller. Derives from ControllerBase rather than InvoiceBaseController, whose route prefix would move the path away from the one emailed links point at.
CustomInvoicePayController::GetPaySummar: What the buyer's pay page shows: the invoice number, the billed record's name, billed lines, balance and whether it can be paid online now. Carries nothing about who is billed. The invoice id carried by the buyer's pay link. Cancels the request. The pay summary, or not found alike for an unknown id, a ticket order and a custom invoice of a module that cannot be collected online.
CustomInvoicePayController::StartPayment: Starts, or hands back, the card payment for the invoice's outstanding balance. Reaches Stripe on an anonymous caller's behalf, so it is bot-challenged like the cart checkout intent. The invoice id carried by the buyer's pay link. Cancels the request. The intent's client secret and id, or a plain failure message.
AlertController: Organizer composing alerts for its own members.
AlertInboxController: The receiving end. Serves whoever is signed in: organizer staff see alerts sent to their organizer, members see alerts sent to them. No permission key, because reading your own alerts is not a grantable capability.
MemberDocumentController: The receiving end of document categories. Read-only by construction: there is no write action here, so a member can browse and download but never modify. No permission key, because reading the documents shared with you is not a grantable capability - the audience rules in the service are the gate.
CustomInvoiceController::Create: Authors a custom invoice against a record of any offered module the signed-in organizer owns. The invoice to create: module and record, category, buyer, due date and billed lines. Cancels the request. The new invoice's public id, or a failure the caller can surface.
CustomInvoiceController::GetList: Lists the signed-in organizer's custom invoices of every module, newest first, filtered, counted and paged on the server. Gated by the existing invoice list permission, so no new key needs seeding. The module, category, statuses, search term and page. Cancels the request. One page of invoices with the total count.
CustomInvoiceController::GetListFilterOp: Reads the choices the custom invoice list's filters offer: the modules the signed-in organizer has invoices in and the organizer's categories. Gated by the same permission as the list it serves. Cancels the request. The module and category filter options.
CustomInvoiceController::SearchEntities: Searches the signed-in organizer's own, live records of one module that a new custom invoice may bill, one page at a time, as the editor's type-ahead dropdown asks for them. The module, the search term and the page. Cancels the request. One page of billable records with the total count, or a failure when the module is missing or not offered.
CustomInvoiceController::SearchLinkCandi: Searches the signed-in organizer's custom invoices of one module that an invoice may link to, one page at a time, newest first, as the editor's link picker asks for them. The module, the search term, the page and the invoice being edited, if any. Cancels the request. One page of link candidates with the total count, or a failure when the module is missing.
CustomInvoiceController::Update: Edits a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns while it is still awaiting its first payment. The module and record it bills cannot be changed. The public id of the invoice to edit. The replacement category, buyer, due date, notes and billed lines. Cancels the request. Success, or a failure the caller can surface when the invoice is not owned, locked, moved or invalid.
CustomInvoiceController::GetForEdit: Loads a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns, in the shape its edit form needs. The public id of the invoice to load. Cancels the request. The invoice's binding, editable fields and lines, or a failure when the caller does not own it.
CustomInvoiceController::GetDetail: Reads the detail of a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns, whatever module it bills. The public id of the invoice to read. Cancels the request. The invoice's detail, or a failure when the caller does not own a custom invoice with that id.
CustomInvoiceController::AddNote: Records a note on a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns. The public id of the invoice to note. The note; required and at most 400 characters. Cancels the request. Success, or a failure the caller can surface when the note is blank or the invoice is not owned.
CustomInvoiceController::Link: Links a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns to another custom invoice they own. The public id of the source invoice the link starts from. Names the target invoice to link to. Cancels the request. Success, or a failure the caller can surface when either invoice is not owned or a link rule is broken.
CustomInvoiceController::Unlink: Removes the link from a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns, clearing both sides. The public id of the invoice to unlink. Cancels the request. Success, or a failure the caller can surface when the invoice is not owned or is not linked.
CustomInvoiceController::CreatePaymentLi: Opens an online card payment for a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns. The public id of the custom invoice to collect. Cancels the request. The Stripe intent's client secret and id, or a failure the caller can surface.
CustomInvoiceController::Send: Emails a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns to its buyer, with the link to pay it online. The public id of the custom invoice to send. Cancels the request. Success once the email is queued, or a failure the caller can surface when it cannot be sent.
CustomInvoiceController::MarkPaid: Records a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns as paid in full outside the gateway. The public id of the custom invoice to settle. Cancels the request. Success, or a failure the caller can surface when the invoice is not owned, not settleable, or a payment is in progress.
CustomInvoiceController::Cancel: Cancels a custom invoice the signed-in organizer owns, recording why on its note trail. The public id of the custom invoice to cancel. The cancellation notes; required and at most 400 characters. Cancels the request. Success, or a failure the caller can surface when the notes are blank, the invoice is not owned, or it cannot be cancelled.
CustomInvoiceEnabledModulesController::G: Lists the modules organizers may author new custom invoices for, as the platform admin has set them. Cancels the request. The enabled module names in module order; an empty list when no module offers custom invoicing.
EventInvoiceController::CancelInvoice: Cancels an event invoice the signed-in organizer owns, recording why on its note trail. The public id of the invoice to cancel. The cancellation notes; required and at most 400 characters. Cancels the request. Success, or a failure the caller can surface when the notes are blank, the invoice is not owned, or it is no longer awaiting payment.
EventTicketCheckInController: The door. Event and session travel in the route rather than the body so a scan can only ever be applied to the session the operator opened, whatever the scanned payload happens to contain.
InvoiceCategoryController::GetList: Lists the signed-in organizer's invoice categories, one page at a time. Paging, sorting and the optional name search term. Cancels the request. The requested page; empty when the organizer has no matching categories.
InvoiceCategoryController::Create: Creates an invoice category owned by the signed-in organizer. The category name, active flag and display order. Cancels the request. The new category's public id, or the validation failure.
InvoiceCategoryController::Update: Renames a category the signed-in organizer owns and applies its active flag and display order. The public id of the category to update. The new name, active flag and display order. Cancels the request. Success, or not-found / validation failure with nothing changed.
InvoiceCategoryController::Delete: Soft-deletes a category the signed-in organizer owns; invoices already billed under it keep it. The public id of the category to delete. Cancels the request. Success, or not-found with nothing changed.
OrganizerNotificationsController::GetSum: Returns Total / Read / Unread counts for the notification tile.
OrganizerNotificationsController::Poll: Polling endpoint — call every 30-60 s to get unread notifications. Returns only notifications the organizer has not yet read.
OrganizerNotificationsController::GetNot: Paginated list of all notifications for the organizer (read + unread). Supports View and Delete actions per row.
OrganizerNotificationsController::GetDet: View a single notification by its recipient record ID. Automatically marks it as read on first open.
OrganizerNotificationsController::MarkAs: Explicitly mark a notification as read.
OrganizerNotificationsController::Delete: Delete a notification from the organizer's view.
AlertEmailWebhookController: Receives Brevo delivery events. Anonymous by necessity, so it is gated on a shared secret configured alongside the webhook in the Brevo dashboard.
